title: 9. Both Sides of the Aisle, Likely Outcomes & No-FOMO Action Plan
book_title: Chapter 9. Both Sides of the Aisle, Likely Outcomes & No-FOMO Action Plan
question: Balancing TXN's 300mm compounder moat against its Stage 4 breakdown and updated risks, what is the honest verdict for existing shares and new capital?

epigraph.quote: Great businesses deserve permanent watchlist space, never permanent exposure when both their 200-day trendline and the broader market break down.
epigraph.author: Institutional Underwriting Desk

web_blocks.html: Bringing Chapters 1 through 8 together requires separating business quality from stock ownership in a broken tape. On fundamental franchise durability, Texas Instruments still earns COMPOUNDER_PASS with PASS_WITH_WATCH on KPIs. Its 300mm wafer cost edge, 22.04% ROIC, 64.2% Q3 gross margin, and 35% OBBBA Investment Tax Credit support long-term cash generation.[2][12][27] On price, balance-sheet risk, and market structure, however, TXN closed November 20 at $263.75 in a STAGE_4 breakdown beneath its 50D ($286.38) and 200D ($266.37) SMAs during a 10-distribution-day US Downtrend.[13][15] Even at $263.75, pro-forma EV ($246.53B) still discounts 10.0% 10-year FCF compounding post-Silicon Labs. We steelman both sides before executing.

Deal closes smoothly in H1 2027, adds IoT wireless scale, and captures $450M of 300mm synergies while $10.13B pro-forma cash handles the $7.5B purchase.
Regulatory delays trigger the $499M reverse break fee and 101% Special Mandatory Redemption on the Nov 9 $2.0B notes, or $15.65B gross debt ($5B term loan) stalls buybacks.
U.S. 300mm supply chain wins Western auto, factory, and AI data-center sockets that value 15-year supply security over lowest spot pricing.
China HQ sales (23% in Q3, +36.6% YoY), ~50% physical China shipments, and Silicon Labs' 30.9% China / 20.0% Taiwan mix face tariffs or local analog share loss.
22.64x Forward P/E and 2.19% yield attract long-only funds once the S&P 500 exits Downtrend and TXN builds a Stage 1 base.
10-distribution-day Downtrend and Semiconductor Rank #21 (17% > 50D EMA) push TXN toward 19x Forward EPS ($220) as funds dump broken 200D averages.
web_blocks.takeaway: The Bull case relies on 2027–2028 FCF inflection and OBBBA tax support; the Bear case combines China trade concentration (50% ship-to / 30.9% SLAB), 12% customer concentration, and Stage 4 institutional liquidation.

web_blocks.html:
Three-Horizon Investment Judgment:
1. Short-Term Trading / Momentum (1–12 weeks): REJECTED (TREND). TXN broke its 50D ($286.38), 30W ($285.65), 200D ($266.37), and 40W ($264.22) moving averages on 1.99x–2.49x volume in a 10-distribution-day Downtrend, with 4H RSI at 29.16 and NO_OPTIONS_EDGE.[13][15][16]
2. Medium-Term Inflection (3–18 months): REJECTED (VALUATION, TREND). Even at $263.75, TXN implies a 10.0% 10-year FCF CAGR post-Silicon Labs while facing $499M merger break-fee risk, ~50% physical China exposure, and a 12% single Analog buyer.[31][32][33]
3. Long-Term Compounding (3–10 years): COMPOUNDER_PASS ON WATCHLIST ONLY (TIER_0 today). Keep TXN on the fundamental monitor list for $225.00–$240.00 conditional watch support (valid at 8.5%–9.5% WACC; Base DCF falls to $198.28 at 10.5% CAPM WACC) once a multi-week Stage 1 base and Stage 2 breakout form.

Existing Position Action (Schwab Account): EXIT_IMMEDIATELY (Sell all 6.7226 shares). Our portfolio holds 6.7226 shares of TXN in schwab at a $1,999.97 cost basis (~$297.50/sh), worth $1,773.09 at $263.75 (-$226.88 / -11.34% unrealized loss, 2.36% weight of $75,110.60 NAV, 1.68 beta, 0 options).[17] Our prior structural stop of $262.00 guarded the 200D SMA and 40W EMA. Both averages broke on November 20 on 16.82M distribution shares, leaving a tiny $1.75 (0.12x ATR14) margin before $262.00. Waiting for a 66-basis-point tick inside a 10-distribution-day Downtrend invites gap risk toward $248–$254. We exit all 6.7226 shares immediately into 100% cash.

web_blocks.title: Final Underwriting Verdict: COMPOUNDER_PASS | REJECTED (TREND, VALUATION) | EXIT_IMMEDIATELY
paragraphs: Respect the 200-day and 40-week breakdown. Sell all 6.7226 Schwab shares (~$1,773.09) immediately into 100% cash, set new capital to REJECTED (TIER_0), and revisit TXN only after a durable Stage 1 base forms.

book_paragraphs: Every institutional dossier must answer a hard question at the finish line: when a great business breaks its chart, do you rationalize holding on, or do you honor your risk rules? On fundamental durability, Texas Instruments remains an unmistakable COMPOUNDER_PASS, carrying a PASS_WITH_WATCH flag on KPI health. Its 300mm cost edge, 22.04% return on invested capital, 64.2% third-quarter gross margin, and 35% OBBBA Investment Tax Credit give it an enduring competitive franchise.

Yet owning a stock is very different from admiring a factory. Let us weigh both sides of the ledger honestly. On the bull side, if capital spending stays within $2 billion to $3 billion while 35% tax credits and $2.14 billion of CHIPS receivables flow in, ex-CHIPS free cash flow could compound above $9 billion to $11 billion—supporting a $350.00 bull target once Silicon Labs closes and delivers our analyst-modeled $450 million of 300mm synergies.

On the bear side, our Pass 1 audit and live market breakdown exposed a denser cluster of risks than our prior report recognized. One unnamed Analog customer accounts for 12% of revenue. Products physically shipped into China represent roughly 50% of sales, while China-headquartered revenue jumped 36.6% YoY to 23% in Q3 2026—and Silicon Labs brings another 30.9% China and 20.0% Taiwan exposure alongside a $499 million regulatory reverse termination fee. Should industrial restocking stall or trade policy bite, depressed margins and 19x forward multiples point toward $220.00.

Assigning 20% probability to our $350.00 Bull Case, 45% to our $295.00 Base Case, and 35% to our $220.00 Bear Case yields a probability-weighted 12-month fair value of $279.75—only +6.07% above Friday's $263.75 close. Against 4.76% two-year and 5.04% ten-year Treasury yields inside a 10-distribution-day market Downtrend, a +6.07% expected equity return offers virtually zero risk premium.

book_subsections.title: EXIT_IMMEDIATELY on 6.7226 Schwab Shares & 100% Cash Redeployment
paragraphs: That math leads straight to two decisive actions. First, on existing holdings: our Schwab account holds 6.7226 shares at a $1,999.97 cost basis (~$297.50 per share), valued at $1,773.09 on November 20 (-$226.88 unrealized loss, 2.36% portfolio weight, 1.68 beta). Our prior $262.00 stop was explicitly designed to protect capital below the 200-day SMA and 40-week EMA. On Friday, TXN closed at $263.75—already below its 200-day SMA ($266.37) and 40-week EMA ($264.22) on 16.82 million shares—leaving just $1.75 (0.12x ATR14) before $262.00. Rather than waiting for a weekend gap through $262.00, we set holding_action to EXIT_IMMEDIATELY and sell all 6.7226 shares into cash.

Second, on new capital: we downgrade TXN from WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT to REJECTED (TIER_0) on both TREND and VALUATION. Why not hide behind WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT? Because TXN is actively falling in STAGE_4 with NO_OPTIONS_EDGE, a 29.16 4-hour RSI showing zero reversal turn, and a $246.53 billion enterprise value that still demands a 10.0% ten-year FCF CAGR post-Silicon Labs. Calling a falling knife a watchlist buy only creates anchoring bias. If TXN later builds a multi-week Stage 1 base near our conditional $225.00 to $240.00 watch band (valid at 8.5%–9.5% WACC, vs. $198.28 Base DCF at 10.5% CAPM WACC) and reclaims its 50-day moving average ($286.38) as market breadth heals, we can re-underwrite it with fresh eyes.

Finally, our 100%-reconciled capital redeployment plan parks all $1,773.09 of TXN exit proceeds into USD Cash and Treasury bills (yielding ~4.76%). We evaluate shortlist compounder Eli Lilly (LLY at $1,347.11, Stage 2, $1,660.00 target, 2.08:1 support R:R) and hold it at 0% today because it trades above its $1,282.61–$1,321.67 support shelf inside a 10-distribution-day Downtrend. We also evaluate outside peer NXP Semiconductors (NXPI at $235.15, $280.00 target) and hold it at 0% because it also sits in STAGE_4 beneath its 50-day and 200-day averages. In a Downtrend, cash is an active, disciplined position.

book_callouts.title: Why We Exit at $263.75 Instead of Waiting for $262.00
book_callouts.text: The $262.00 stop existed to guard the 200D SMA and 40W EMA. Now that both averages broke on 2x volume in a 10-distribution-day Downtrend, holding for the last $1.75 (0.12 ATRs) adds pure gap risk. Selling 6.7226 shares locks in a small -30 bps portfolio loss and moves 100% into ~4.76% cash.
